title: Trump’s Giant Arch Plan Hits a Speed Bump: Too Tall for Washington’s Rules!
summary:
Imagine a huge arch, taller than a 20-story building, rising up right next to the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. That’s what President Donald Trump wants to build! But there’s a catch: a group called the National Capital Planning Commission is looking at the plan today, and their staff says the arch is too tall for the city’s rules.

Washington, D.C. has a special law called the Height of Buildings Act. It keeps buildings from getting too high so the city’s famous skyline stays beautiful. The arch would be 250 feet (76 meters) tall — that’s more than twice as tall as the Lincoln Memorial, which is only 99 feet! The planning commission’s staff says the design needs to be changed to follow the law. They want the builders to move some of the height around, maybe by making the statues on top shorter or changing the roof. But even with those changes, the arch could still reach 250 feet.

The arch would sit on a traffic circle in Virginia, right across the Memorial Bridge from Washington, D.C. Some people are upset because they think it will block the view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. That view was meant to show how the North and South came back together after the Civil War. A group of veterans and a historian have even gone to court to try to stop the arch.

But Trump has friends on the commission. He put his top aide, Will Scharf, in charge. Another group, the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts, already said yes to the design in May. The planning commission will decide if the project can move forward, but first they want more details about traffic, the granite outside, and other things. No one knows yet how much the arch will cost, but Trump once said he might use leftover money from a White House ballroom project. The hearing is happening today at 1 p.m. — we’ll see what happens next!
why_it_matters: Even exciting building ideas must follow rules that protect a city’s history and beauty, showing how communities balance big dreams with keeping special places the same for future generations.

background_read: Washington, D.C. has a law called the Height of Buildings Act that limits how tall buildings can be so the city keeps its historic skyline. The Lincoln Memorial (a monument honoring President Abraham Lincoln) and Arlington National Cemetery (a burial place for soldiers) are two of the most important sites in the area.
The view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery was designed to symbolize the reuniting of the North and South after the Civil War, a war that divided the country in the 1860s.
The National Capital Planning Commission is a group that reviews big building projects near Washington’s landmarks before they can be built.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, the National Capital Planning Commission, Will Scharf (Trump’s top aide), and veterans and a historian.
WHAT: Trump wants to build a 250‑foot arch, but the planning commission says it’s too tall for the city’s height law.
WHERE: On a traffic circle in Virginia, right across the Memorial Bridge from Washington, D.C., near the Lincoln Memorial.

WHY: The arch would be more than twice as tall as the Lincoln Memorial and could block a historic view, breaking the Height of Buildings Act and upsetting people who want to protect the area’s symbolism.

perspectives.description: They want to build a grand, eye-catching arch as a lasting monument, believing it would honor the nation in a big way.
They are concerned that the arch is too tall and would break the Height of Buildings Act, so they want the design changed to follow the law.
They are upset because the arch could block the symbolic view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, which was meant to show how the country came together after the Civil War.
